title: "Logistic Regression Classifier"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates multiclass logistic regression with an intercept using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Data

```{r data}
X <- matrix(
  c(
    -0.73018489, -0.77691935, -0.5531103, -0.53005191, -0.29156667,
     0.1168031, -1.40480427, -0.33364746, -1.12263088, -1.48629103,
    -0.86543502, -1.12070302, -0.9318949,  0.07586872, -0.66288856,
     0.18171725, -0.737435,   0.22143158, -0.37855445,  0.99452555,
    -0.11916944,  0.42473491,  1.08249098,  0.3675828,   0.45179015,
     1.99695757,  2.88362735, -0.45059391,  1.60981248, -0.72399731,
     0.79898074,  2.11187681, -1.43869773, -1.76823514,  2.48784366,
     2.44513227,  0.07709601,  2.87190709,  0.05356797,  0.5230911,
     1.01352685, -1.11759934, -0.75510393,  0.36976656, -1.71651458,
    -0.67448552,  1.98517725,  0.56222941,  0.07899979,  1.76713307
  ),
  nrow = 25, ncol = 2
)

labels <- c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0,
            1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2, 2, 1)
```

## Train/Test Split

```{r split}
result <- train_test_split(X, labels, test_size = 0.2, seed = 2001L)
X_train <- result[[1]]
X_test <- result[[2]]
labels_train <- result[[3]]
labels_test <- result[[4]]
```

## Fit

```{r fit}
clss <- linmod$new("logistic", intercept = TRUE)
clss$fit(X_train, labels_train)
```

## Score

```{r score}
acc <- clss$score(X_train, labels_train)
cat(sprintf("Training accuracy: %.3f\n", acc))
cat("Expected          : ~0.75\n")
```

## Predict

```{r predict}
pred <- clss$predict(X_test)

cat("Predictions vs Expected:\n")
for (i in seq_along(pred)) {
  cat(sprintf("  predicted %d    expected %d\n", as.integer(pred[i]), as.integer(labels_test[i])))
}
```
